title: Learning the exogenous rate but not the distance to criticality in nearly unstable heavy-tailed Hawkes processes
summary: In the nearly unstable heavy-tailed regime of Jaisson and Rosenbaum, where the intensity of a linear Hawkes process converges to a rough square-root Volterra process, we ask what a record of length $T$ reveals about the relative distance to criticality $1-ρ$ and the exogenous rate $μ$. For the first, the information is governed by $\mathcal I_T=Tμ(1-ρ)$, not by the number of events; $\mathcal I_T$ stays bounded although the event count diverges like $T^{2γ}$, so no estimator of the relative distance to criticality is uniformly locally consistent.
